N-1.1-A.skill: recognize a statistical question (one that anticipates variability in data) among questions that have a single fixed answer.

N-1.1-B.skill: identify the population of interest from an investigative question and judge what a sample taken from a different group can support.

N-1.2-A.skill: classify variables in a data set, recognizing numeric identifiers and ordered categories as categorical and counts as quantitative.

N-1.2-B.skill: identify the individuals and the type of each variable in a described data set, where one variable summarizes many subjects as a percentage.

N-1.3-A.skill: use a relative frequency and a count to recover the total of a categorical table, then find a conditional percentage among a subset of categories.

N-1.3-B.skill: compare two groups of different sizes using relative frequencies, and distinguish a difference in percentage points from a relative difference or a difference in counts.

N-1.4-A.skill: evaluate a claim drawn from a bar chart whose vertical axis does not start at zero, comparing visual height with the actual counts.

N-1.4-B.skill: choose a display for a categorical variable that allows multiple responses, recognizing when a pie chart is inappropriate.

N-1.5-A.skill: locate the interval containing the median from the bar heights of a histogram, avoiding the tallest-bar and axis-midpoint errors.

N-1.5-B.skill: read a relative frequency histogram, first recovering the sample size from two bars and then converting percentages of a subset of bins into a count.

N-1.6-A.skill: choose the description of a quantitative distribution that has shape, resistant center and spread, and unusual features, stated in context.

N-1.6-B.skill: interpret a bimodal distribution, recognizing that a single mean can fall where few observations lie and that the data may mix two subgroups.

N-1.7-A.skill: determine how a linear change of units (multiply then add) changes the mean and standard deviation.

N-1.7-B.skill: find and interpret the mean of a combined group from the means and sizes of two subgroups, avoiding the unweighted average of the means.
